items.summary: The Court of International Trade sustained the Department of Commerce's determination that CS Wind Malaysia received a countervailable benefit from Malaysian import duty exemptions, holding that the full value of such exemptions is presumed to confer a benefit unless the foreign government demonstrates reasonable systems to track consumed inputs. The court remanded the Department's analysis of rental rates for a property lease from the Malaysian government and CS Wind's request for an entered-value adjustment for further reconsideration.

and

Before: M. Mill
items.summary: The Court of International Trade sustained the Department of Commerce's redetermination on remand regarding rental rates for CS Wind's property lease from the Malaysian government and the company's request for an entered-value adjustment. Commerce reaffirmed its use of averaged land pricing data from multiple sources and maintained that insufficient customs documentation and mismatches between invoice values and customs forms did not support the adjustment.

items.summary: This executive order implements the Lindsey O. Graham Sanctioning Russia and Iran Act of 2026, which was signed into law on September 18, 2026. The order increases duty rates by 500 percent on goods from the Russian Federation and 100 percent on goods from the five largest importers of Russian crude oil and natural gas and from the top five facilitators of Russian oil sanctions evasion, subject to exceptions and waivers specified in the Graham Act. The order delegates implementation and monitoring responsibilities to the Trade Representative, State Department, Treasury Department, and Energy Department, and waives application of certain sanctions provisions and duties under the Graham Act.
items.title: Implementing the Lindsey O. Graham Sanctioning Russia and Iran Act of 2026

items.summary: The Sixth Circuit Court of Appeals denied a petition for review of a Board of Immigration Appeals decision denying asylum protection to Baichao Li, a Chinese national who claimed persecution based on his conversion to Christianity. The court found the agency's credibility and corroboration findings were supported by substantial evidence, noting significant inconsistencies between Li's testimony and his supporting documentation regarding dates and injury details.
items.title: Baichao Li v. Todd Blanche

items.summary: The Sixth Circuit Court of Appeals affirmed a 70-month sentence for Tony Johnson, rejecting his challenge to a sentencing enhancement for possessing a firearm in connection with drug trafficking. The court found the district court did not clearly err in concluding that a nexus existed between the firearm and Johnson's drug trafficking based on the weapons being found in close proximity to multiple controlled substances.
items.title: USA v. Tony Johnson

items.summary: The Sixth Circuit Court of Appeals affirmed dismissal of a Second Amendment challenge to the felon-in-possession statute brought by Dalonta Crudup, who purchased firearms while holding prior felony convictions for drug and firearm offenses. The court determined that Crudup failed to demonstrate he is not a dangerous individual whom Congress may disarm, and found his criminal record supported such a finding.
items.title: USA v. Dalonta Crudup

items.summary: The Sixth Circuit Court of Appeals affirmed a 144-month sentence for Rose Rhear in a methamphetamine conspiracy case, rejecting her argument that the government breached her plea agreement by failing to object to a higher drug quantity finding at sentencing. The court found the government adequately communicated its agreement with the drug quantity specified in the plea agreement through its statements regarding correct sentencing calculations.
items.title: USA v. Rose Rhear

The plaintiffs' claims regarding breach of a loan agreement also failed because the agreement did not create third-party beneficiary rights for the construction company.

items.summary: The Sixth Circuit Court of Appeals affirmed the district court's dismissal of breach-of-contract claims against Travelers Insurance Company and I.E. Development, LLC for lack of privity of contract, dismissal of negligence claims for failure to allege duties independent of contractual obligations, and grant of summary judgment to Northfield Insurance Company on M32's remaining breach-of-contract claim based on res judicata. The judgment in the related declaratory judgment action precluded further litigation regarding the policy rescission and M32's insurance claim denial.
items.title: Michigan 32, LLC, et al v. Travelers Insurance Company, et al

items.summary: The Sixth Circuit Court of Appeals denied a petition for review of the Board of Immigration Appeals' denial of asylum and withholding of removal to Gerson Rosales-Camaja, a Guatemalan national who fled after gang members threatened him. The Board found that Rosales-Camaja failed to demonstrate that the Guatemalan government was unable or unwilling to protect him from gang violence, noting that he did not alert police at the time of the threats. The court affirmed the Board's finding that no reasonable adjudicator would be compelled to reach a contrary conclusion.
items.title: Gerson Rosales-Camaja v. Todd Blanche

items.summary: The Sixth Circuit Court of Appeals affirmed an above-guidelines sentence of 30 months imposed on Dennis Martinez-Cacho for illegal reentry in violation of 8 U.S.C. § 1326. The district court imposed the upward variance based on Martinez-Cacho's pattern of domestic violence toward women and his quick reentry to the United States after his deportation in January 2022. The court rejected Martinez-Cacho's arguments that his sentence was substantively and procedurally unreasonable.
items.title: USA v. Dennis Martinez-Cacho

items.summary: The Sixth Circuit Court of Appeals affirmed in part a district court's denial of qualified immunity and governmental immunity to nine defendants in a case where current and former inmates alleged that pervasive mold at the Women's Huron Valley Correctional Facility caused serious health harms in violation of the Eighth Amendment and Michigan law. The court reversed as to five defendants due to conclusory allegations lacking factual basis. The case involves claims of institutional failure to abate mold and alleged concealment by correctional officials.
items.title: Paula Bailey, et al v. MDOC, et al

items.summary: The Sixth Circuit Court of Appeals affirmed the district court's grant of summary judgment permitting Northfield Insurance Company to rescind a commercial property insurance policy issued to Michigan 32, LLC based on the company's material misrepresentation in its application that it maintained a policy-compliant fire alarm when no such alarm existed. The policy was rendered void ab initio, and the court rejected M32's waiver and estoppel defenses. Northfield refunded the policy premium after denying M32's claim for damages from a 2023 fire.
items.title: Northfield Insurance Company v. Michigan 32, LLC

items.opening_verbatim: Public Law 119–121: To amend the Visit America Act to promote music tourism, and for other purposes. Public Law 121 Public Law 119–121 140 Stat. 1067 2026-10-09 2026-10-09 United States Government Publishing Office National Archives and Rec
items.summary: Public Law 119-121 amends the Visit America Act to establish music tourism promotion as a responsibility of the Assistant Secretary of Commerce for Travel and Tourism, effective October 9, 2026. The law defines music tourism as travel to visit music-related attractions or to attend music festivals and concerts, and requires the Assistant Secretary to identify and promote music tourism locations and events for domestic and international travel. The Assistant Secretary is required to submit biennial reports to Congress on activities, findings, achievements, and vulnerabilities relating to these music tourism goals.
items.title: Public Law 119–121: To amend the Visit America Act to promote music tourism, and for other purposes.

items.opening_verbatim: ENVIRONMENTAL PROTECTION AGENCY 40 CFR Parts 80 and 1090 [EPA-HQ-OAR-2024-0505; FRL-11947.2-01-OAR] RIN 2060-AX09 Renewable Fuel Standard (RFS) Program: Reallocation of Additional 2025 Small Refinery Exemptions AGENCY: Environmental Protect
items.summary: The U.S. Environmental Protection Agency (EPA) is co-proposing two approaches to revising the existing 2026 and 2027 small refinery exemption (SRE) reallocation volumes under the Renewable Fuel Standard (RFS) program in response to a higher volume of 2025 SREs than previously projected when the Agency set the renewable fuel volumes and percentage standards on April 1, 2026. One approach would reallocate the additional 2025 SRE volume equally between the 2026 and 2027 SRE reallocation volumes, while the other approach would reallocate all the additional 2025 SRE volume to the 2027 SRE reallocation volume. Additionally, given the proposed revision to the 2026 standards, this proposed action may extend the existing 2026 compliance reporting deadline of March 31, 2027.
items.title: Renewable Fuel Standard (RFS) Program: Reallocation of Additional 2025 Small Refinery Exemptions

items.summary: The Coast Guard is establishing a temporary special local regulation (SLR) for certain navigable waters of Lake Havasu. This action is necessary to provide for the safety of life on these navigable waters near Lake Havasu City, AZ during the Pineapple Races event beginning at 3 p.m. on October 20, 2026, and ending the evening of October 20, 2026, at 8 p.m. This regulation prohibits persons and vessels from entering the regulated area unless specifically authorized by the Captain of the Port San Diego or their designated representative.
items.title: Special Local Regulation; Lake Havasu, Lake Havasu City, AZ

items.summary: The Coast Guard is establishing a temporary safety zone for navigable waters within 200 yards of location 18°19′25.42″ N, 065°19′43.55″ W, adjacent to Playa Tamarindo Grande Beach, Culebra, Puerto Rico. The safety zone is needed to protect personnel, vessels, and the marine environment from potential hazards associated with unexploded ordnance and associated removal operations. Entry of vessels or persons into this zone is prohibited unless specifically authorized by the Captain of the Port, Sector San Juan, or their designated representative.

items.opening_verbatim: DEPARTMENT OF THE INTERIOR National Park Service 36 CFR Part 13 [NPS-DENA-NPS0043926; PPAKDENAS0, PPMPSPD1Z.YM0000] RIN 1024-AF11 Denali National Park and Preserve; Vehicle Use AGENCY: National Park Service, Interior. ACTION: Final rule. SU
items.summary: The National Park Service (NPS) amends special regulations for Denali National Park and Preserve to conform the regulations regarding the number of vehicles that can travel on the restricted section of the Denali Park Road (miles 15-90) to a Vehicle Management Plan that the NPS has been implementing since 2012. This rule implements the plan's limit that no more than 160 vehicles may travel on the restricted section of the road per 24-hour period during the visitor season (also referred to as the “allocation season”), defined in the park's General Management Plan as beginning on the Saturday before Memorial Day and ending on the second Thursday after Labor Day. This limit allows the NPS to meet growing visitor demand while maintaining a high-quality experience for visitors.
items.title: Denali National Park and Preserve; Vehicle Use

items.summary: The Coast Guard is proposing to establish a temporary safety zone for navigable waters on the Cumberland River from mile marker 221.7 to 222. items.summary: This executive order implements the Lindsey O. Graham Sanctioning Russia and Iran Act of 2026, which was signed into law on September 18, 2026. The order increases duty rates by 500 percent on goods from the Russian Federation and 100 percent on goods from the five largest importers of Russian crude oil and natural gas and from the top five facilitators of Russian oil sanctions evasion, subject to exceptions and waivers specified in the Graham Act. The order delegates implementation and monitoring responsibilities to the Trade Representative, State Department, Treasury Department, and Energy Department, and waives application of certain sanctions provisions and duties under the Graham Act.
